prompt:
You are a developer-relations researcher at a company that turns SaaS apps into tools AI agents can call.
Research ONE app and fill a strict JSON schema. Use web search. Prefer the vendor's own developer docs,
API reference, pricing page, and app-review/partner pages over blogs or aggregators.

App: Freshdesk
Category: Support and Helpdesk
Hint (may be misleading, verify it): freshdesk.com

Rules
1. Every field is an object: {"value": ..., "confidence": "high|med|low", "source_url": "..."}.
2. source_url must be a page you actually saw in search results for THIS field. Never construct or guess a URL.
   If you did not find one, set value "unknown", confidence "low", source_url null.
3. "unknown" is a correct, rewarded answer. An invented answer is the worst possible answer.
4. access_path = the most restrictive step needed to use the API in production, not just to read docs.
   Self-serve OAuth client + mandatory app review for production scopes => "app_review_required".
   Free docs but the useful endpoints need a paid plan => "paid_plan_required".
5. If the thing is a command-line tool or library with no hosted API, use api_type "cli_only",
   auth_methods ["none"], access_path "not_applicable_local", toolkit_bucket "local_or_sandbox_toolkit".
6. If the hint names a different product than the app (e.g. a parent platform), research the app itself and say so in main_blocker.
7. "OAuth requested" or "coming soon" is NOT shipped. Only report auth that is documented as available.
8. official_mcp = "official" only if the vendor itself publishes or documents the MCP server.
9. confidence: high = stated explicitly on a vendor docs page; med = inferred from vendor pages; low = third-party or memory.

Allowed enums
auth_methods (array): oauth2, api_key, basic, bearer_token, jwt, hmac_signature, session_login, none, unknown
access_path: self_serve_free, self_serve_trial, paid_plan_required, app_review_required, partner_or_sales_gated, no_public_api, not_applicable_local, unknown
api_type: rest, graphql, rest_and_graphql, rpc_or_sdk_only, cli_only, none, unknown
api_breadth: broad (CRUD across many objects), narrow (a few resources), single_endpoint, none, unknown
official_mcp: official, community_only, none_found, unknown
base_url_model: fixed, per_tenant_subdomain, self_hosted_or_customer_host, regional, not_applicable, unknown
toolkit_bucket: remote_api_toolkit, local_or_sandbox_toolkit, wrap_existing_mcp, not_buildable_yet, unknown
docs_quality: full_public_reference, partial_or_thin, none_public, unknown
test_account: free_tier_or_sandbox, trial_only, none, unknown

Return ONLY this JSON, no prose, no markdown fences:
{
  "one_liner": {...},        // what it does, max 15 words
  "auth_methods": {...},
  "access_path": {...},
  "api_type": {...},
  "api_breadth": {...},
  "official_mcp": {...},
  "base_url_model": {...},
  "toolkit_bucket": {...},
  "docs_quality": {...},
  "test_account": {...},
  "main_blocker": {...},     // one sentence; "none" if buildable today
  "docs_url": {...}          // primary API reference URL
}

## Official Freshdesk MCP Server

The Freshworks Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enables AI tools like Cursor and Claude to securely connect and interact with Freshdesk. Starting September 10, 2026, the Freshworks MCP integration is generally available.

## Community-Built Alternatives

There are also several community-built MCP servers for Freshdesk available:

- Freshdesk is a community-built MCP server published by effytech that provides AI assistants with tools and capabilities via the Model Context Protocol. It's an MCP server implementation that integrates with Freshdesk, enabling AI models to interact with Freshdesk modules and perform various support operations.

- MCP server for Freshdesk provides: tickets, contacts, companies, agents, groups, and knowledge base.

- A production-ready Freshdesk MCP Server allows AI assistants to search support tickets, retrieve ticket details and conversations, monitor queues and SLA risk, update fields, and add replies or notes while maintaining enterprise security and governance.

The official Freshworks MCP server is now generally available as of September 2026, while various third-party implementations also exist for different integration needs.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Freshdesk API authentication:

## Authentication Method

Freshdesk's v2 REST API uses HTTP Basic Auth with an API key as the username and any non-empty string as the password - there is no OAuth 2.0 for the v2 API.

## API Key

You can find your API key by going to the Profile Settings page in your Freshdesk account. More specifically, click your profile picture in the top-right, choose Profile Settings, and your API key is shown in the right-hand pane.

## Authentication Format

Use HTTP Basic Authentication with your API key as the username and any non-empty string (commonly X) as the password — for example curl -u YOUR_API_KEY:X.

## Important Notes

- There's no OAuth flow; the key alone authorises the request and inherits your agent's permissions.
- An API key is a unique alphanumeric identifier for each agent on your Freshdesk Account.
- Starting 31st August 2021 Freshdesk stopped supporting username and password based authentication and moved to API based authentication as a standard.

The base URL for the API is `https://<your-domain>.freshdesk.com/api/v2/`.

Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding Freshdesk API rate limits and plan restrictions:

## API Rate Limits and Plan Requirements

Freshdesk API rate limits are per-minute and per-account, depending on your plan: roughly 200 calls/min on Growth, 400 on Pro, and 700 on Enterprise, with the Free plan having no API access and trials capped at 50/min.

The Free plan has no API access at all, higher rate limits and per-endpoint headroom require paying up to Pro or Enterprise.

## Plan-Based Rate Limits

The number of API calls you can make is based on your plan. Upgrading your Freshdesk plan typically provides higher Freshdesk API rate limits.

## Additional Information

- Limits are enforced per Freshdesk account, not per API key. Custom apps that consume the API count toward the account total.
- When the limit is breached, responses return HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header indicating wait seconds before retrying.
- If you want to increase the API limit for any of the modules, you can drop an email to support@freshdesk.com
